newsitem.title: USA: Clinton meets with Democrats on budget efforts.
newsitem.headline: Clinton meets with Democrats on budget efforts.

text.p: President Clinton met with Democratic congressional leaders at the White House Wednesday and discussed efforts to flesh out the details of a balanced budget agreement with Republicans.
Senate Democratic leader Tom Daschle said after the meeting that he was "optimistic" an agreement could be reached that would allow Senate committees to begin drafting budget legislation Thursday.
"At least in the Senate, I'm optimistic that the outstanding disagreements are of minor nature and can be resolved," Daschle said while declining to discuss specific details.
House Democrats left the White House without speaking with reporters.
The framework of a plan that would cut taxes and spending and balance the budget by 2002 was agreed on by the president and congressional Republicans May 2, but details were still being negotiated.
Many of Clinton's fellow Democrats are uneasy about the plan, believing it will eviscerate many of the social programmes the party has fought for over the years.
On efforts to limit late-term abortions, Daschle said, "The president is willing to accept my compromise on late-term abortions."

The White House Tuesday said it was "possible" Clinton would support Daschle's compromise, which would ban late-term abortions, except in cases where the woman's life was in danger or where she risked "grievous injury" to her health.

The highly controversial procedure, called partial-birth abortion by its opponents but also known as dilation and extraction, involves the partial extraction of the foetus and the subsequent suctioning out of the foetal brain and removal of the foetus.

The Senate this week is expected to vote on a Republican proposal to ban such procedures except to save the life of the woman. But chief sponsor Rick Santorum, a Pennsylvania Republican, has acknowledged he is about five votes shy of a veto-proof 67 votes.
Clinton vetoed that measure last year and has vowed to do so again.
